title: Find the integrating factor
text: Put the equation in the form $$y'+p\left(x\right) y=q(x)$$, then multiply by the integrating factor so the left side becomes the derivative of the integrating factor times $$y$$.

title: Integrate and solve
text: Dividing by $$\sqrt{x}$$ gives $$y'-\frac{y}{\sqrt{x}}=2\sqrt{x}$$, and the integrating factor is $$e^{\left(-2\sqrt{x}\right)}$$. Substituting $$u=\sqrt{x}$$ in the integral gives $$e^{\left(-2\sqrt{x}\right)} y=-e^{\left(-2\sqrt{x}\right)} \left(2x+2\sqrt{x}+1\right)+C$$. $$y(0)=1$$ gives $$C=2$$.
